thread:
maya: Heads-up — eu-west dedicated-pool-3 showing 5-10x tail latency on small-textgen jobs since ~03:12 UTC. GPU util uneven: one host at ~98% while siblings idle. Thinking noisy neighbor or NIC egress saturation. ops-bot already flagged.

ops-bot: ALERT: high_p99_latency pool=dedi-pool-3 metric=token_latency_p99 value=2.3s (svc=inference-gateway)

kevin: Looking at proxy and host metrics — a handful of pods from tenant `acme-corp` are opening many concurrent short requests + large egress. Could be an embedding job fragmentation. @trevor can you confirm tenant tags?

trevor: Running quick query: `rquery --tenant acme-corp --last 10m --group by pod` shows ~1200 small requests/s spread across 6 pods, 80% hitting gpu-17. So hot-spot.

ella: If gpu-17 is hot we can drain it from the pool and force routing to fallback. Risk: spilling KV cache and warming cost. Command to drain:
```
fleetctl drain --node gpu-17 --pool dedi-pool-3 --grace 30s
```
Will that be enough?

sam: Draining + warmup on other nodes will increase short-term cost. Spinning an isolated slice (1 x A10 + 1 replica) for acme-corp is about ~$500/day. Tradeoff: immediate SLA protection vs cost. :thinking:

maya: Prioritize SLA — spin isolated slice and throttle tenant concurrently. Ops please proceed. I'll open a billing exception ticket.

trevor: Applied soft throttle rule: `qos.set --tenant acme-corp --rps 50 --scope pool` — immediate effect: p99 dropped from 2.3s -> 0.9s within 90s. Still seeing NIC tx queueing on gpu-17.

kevin: Created a canary route (10%) to dedi-pool-4 using quantized-variant to reduce gpu memory & spread load. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: ACTION: new_slice_request id=sr-20240321-78 status=provisioning slice=acme-isolated-01

ella: Drained gpu-17: `fleetctl drain` returned OK, pods rescheduled to pool-4 and the new slice. Cache misses increased but latency stabilized.

sam: FYI cost hit estimate for today with slice + extra reschedules: ~$620. I'll update the billing ticket.

ops-sre: Please drop runbook pointer here once we have a post-incident writeup. Need the root-cause checklist (tenant throttles, NIC policing, pool routing) so we can automate detection.

maya: Agreed. For next steps: 1) keep the isolated slice until end of day; 2) add NIC policing candidate to infra experiments; 3) add a probe to detect >50% p99 variance across nodes in same pool. I'll file the follow-ups. Thanks all.

ops-bot: RESOLVED: host=gpu-17 drained, pool=p99 back to 0.28s, slice=acme-isolated-01 active. Ticket=billing-4321
